text:
olivia: quick design review 14 attached mock shows a compact tutorial overlay that walks users through canary steps when they first open the rollout timeline. thoughts? :eyes:

mike: nice. can the overlay be dismissible per-org? some teams will hate forced tours.

olivia: yes 14 dismissible with a "don't show again" toggle stored in profile prefs. also fades after first successful canary.

sam: from engineering pov, overlay is fine but focus trapping needs care. if keyboard focus gets stuck inside the stepper we break the console shortcuts.

lina: a11y notes: make sure each step uses role="dialog" and aria-labelledby. also announce current step as "step x of y" to screenreaders. avoid using only color to indicate the traffic hotspot.

rebecca: copy nit: step 2 currently says "route 10% to canary" 14 suggest "send 10% of traffic to the canary version" for clarity.

mike: good catch. also for rollback confirm modal: current copy "rollback now?" feels abrupt for non-technical pms. propose: "rollback to previous version 14 your users will receive the last stable variant. confirm rollback?"

olivia: updated copy proposal: "rollback to previous version (undo recent changes). a/b tests will stop and traffic will revert. proceed?" thoughts on length?

lina: shorter is better for screenreaders. maybe: "rollback to previous version. this will stop active experiments and revert traffic. continue?"

sam: ux -> dev tradeoff: we want a small inline changelog snippet in the confirm modal (title + commit hash + author). can we show 1-line summary without making modal heavy?

olivia: mock shows a collapsed summary with chevron to expand. default collapsed: "release: fix/latency - 3 files changed 14 @dana". expand shows diff link.

mike: interaction question: if user hits esc in the overlay, should that close only the overlay or also exit the timeline view? prefer overlay only.

sam: agreed 14 esc closes overlay; timeline keyboard shortcuts still work. we'll add explicit focus restore to the timeline header button.

lina: focus restore must set focus to a visible control (e.g., canary allocation slider) and call focus() after aria-hidden toggles.

rebecca: traffic slider microcopy: current label "allocation" is vague. suggest "canary traffic allocation" and tooltip: "percent of live traffic served by this version."

olivia: ui visual: showing mini sparkline on each version chip for quick health glance 14 ok?

mike: great for product. make sure it's optional per org (perf + visual noise).

sam: perf concern: sparklines will require extra metrics queries. can we lazy-load them? show skeleton then fetch?

olivia: plan: lazy-load after 500ms on expand and cache per session. if metrics unavailable, show dashed placeholder.

lina: color contrast on sparkline must meet aa. avoid thin lines 14 increase stroke to 2px or add subtle fill.

rebecca: final: can we change the tutorial cta from "walk me through" to "show me how"? friendlier.

mike: :thumbsup: love that.

deploy-bot: deploy preview ready: https://preview.redwood.ai/rollout/overlay-steps (build #4821)

sam: i'll test keyboard flow against preview today and report issues.

olivia: thanks all 14 i'll update mocks and post new figma link in this thread when ready.

mike: tagging a follow-up for product review next tue. :calendar:

olivia: linking figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/rollout-overlay-stepper (v3)

sam: noted 2 engineering tasks: focus restore + lazy-load sparklines. adding to sprint board.

lina: i'll write the aria checklist and paste it here once drafted.

rebecca: leaving a small ux note: emphasize clear undo path in copy 14 teams panic on rollbacks. maybe include a link to "rollback docs" in the modal.

olivia: will add docs link and a small secondary line: "you can re-deploy the previous version or contact support for assistance."

mike: cool. end of thread unless blocker found. :white_check_mark:
